utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-A, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances of the parties. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Marwan Dalal for the Prosecution, together with appeals counsel, Barbara Goy, and our case manager, Ms. Alma Imamovic-Ivanov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now for Mr. Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Richard Harvey for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, good afternoon. Rodney Dixon on behalf of Mr. Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Colleen Rohan on behalf of Mr. Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Brahimaj, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT BRAHIMAJ: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is a status conference called in accordance with Article 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and that, as you know, requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The previous Status Conference in this case was held on 22nd August, 2008, so it comes a bit earlier today, but due to the fact that the next Status Conference would have taken place during the judicial recess and considering the scheduling of trials, I thought it was useful to have it today, and so I issued the order on 12 November to have the conference now. Let me recall the situation of the case. The Trial Chamber rendered its judgement in this case on 3 April 2008. The Prosecution filed its notice of appeal on 2nd May, 2008, while counsel for Mr. Brahimaj filed its notice of appeal 5 May 2008. Then the Prosecution filed its appeal brief on 16 July, while Mr. Brahimaj submitted his on 19 of July. Responses and replies followed. As of mid-September, the briefing appears to be complete now in this case. The Appeals Chamber will consider the matters of the appeal in due course and advise about a possible hearing in the future. Is there anything concerning the schedule that the parties want to raise now? That does not seem to be the case. So in light of the rules, I would like to inquire about Mr. Brahimaj's state of health and conditions of detention. Let me recall to you, Mr. Brahimaj, that pursuant to Rules 80 and 81 of the Rules of Detention, if a detainee is not satisfied with the conditions of his or her detention, he or she is entitled to "make a complaint to the Commanding Officer" and, in case of an unsatisfactory response, to "make a written complaint ... to the Registrar, who shall inform the President" of the Tribunal. So I would like to inquire, Mr. Brahimaj, do you have any concerns in relation to your state of health or conditions of detention? THE APPELLANT BRAHIMAJ: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Brahimaj. Well, at this point I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issue they would like to raise at this time. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has nothing to add at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Haradinaj, there's nothing to raise at this point in time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Balaj, the same is true. We have nothing to raise at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one matter to raise on behalf of Mr. Brahimaj. As Your Honour has correctly recalled, the judgement of the Trial Chamber was issued on the 3rd of April. As Your Honour will know, the rules require that a translation should be provided as soon as possible to the defendant. The promised translation is still awaited here in November and approaching December. In September, we wrote to express our concern at the excessive delay and were assured that the final translation would be provided to Mr. Brahimaj by the 7th of November. The 7th of November has been and gone. We have written again requesting further information on why this additional delay. The explanation we have been given is that there is a serious shortage of Albanian interpreters available here at the Tribunal and that one of the interpreters has been working apparently full-time - I'm not quite sure for how much of the time that has been going on - on trying to prepare this. The situation is now that Mr. Brahimaj has other colleagues in the Detention Unit who have copies of his judgement in B/C/S, and he still doesn't have it in his own language. So it's been translated into B/C/S but not into Albanian as we stand here today. I do understand from speaking with OLAD today that the draft of the translation has been completed and the final version is, we are now told, expected shortly, it is hoped by the 7th of December. Well, I have to say, speaking for myself, that hopes have been dashed too many times in the past; and I think - at a minimum, at least - it would be appropriate for my client to be provided with the draft of the translation so that he can see that on the understanding that, of course, it is still only the draft and therefore should not be taken as word-for-word accurate. But at least that would provide him with something to be going on with while the final version is being completed. I understand that this would be possible, but I think it probably requires an order or at least a request from this Chamber so that that can take place. So that is what I ask today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, I thank you for raising this issue. I will look into that matter and see what can be done in order that your client is provided with the translation as quickly as possible, and possibly, as of now, the draft of the translation, if available.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: May I tell the head of the Translation Unit that this Chamber would approve of him being provided with a draft immediately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I have no problem with that, of course, personally. I don't know what are the uses of the Translation Unit because I know interpreters don't like to have provisional translations going out. But I have no problem that your client is provided with a translation. You can certainly tell that. I will tell them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, if there is no other issue to be raised now, I believe this concludes our business today. I thank the parties for their attendance and call the hearing to a close today.
